dataset: Mumbai Stormwater Drainage and River Network (BRIMSTOWAD Master Plan)
sources_checked: Chitale Fact Finding Committee on Mumbai Floods (2006 Comprehensive Final Report)
Brihanmumbai Storm Water Disposal System (BRIMSTOWAD) Project Reports (1993, 2006, 2015)
Maharashtra State Disaster Management Authority (SDMA) Flood Hazard Atlas
Ministry of Housing and Urban Affairs (MoHUA) AMRUT Programme GIS Database
OpenStreetMap waterway (river, stream, canal, drain) and manhole database
Mumbai Metropolitan Region Development Authority (MMRDA) Mithi River Development Project

collected_data.nodes: Major BRIMSTOWAD stormwater pumping stations, lake overflow intake weirs, holding ponds, and critical river junctions with known pump capacities and invert elevations.
collected_data.links: Major drainage rivers (Mithi, Dahisar, Poisar, Oshiwara) and primary trunk storm nullahs (Irla, Chunabhatti) with hydraulic dimensions (width, depth, Manning's roughness, slope).
collected_data.outfalls: 11 critical tidal discharge outfalls into the Arabian Sea, Mahim Bay, and Thane Creek with tidal backflow flap gate status and invert elevations.

missing_data: Micro-scale subterranean pipe network geometry (approx. 2,000+ km of minor roadside underground box drains and cylindrical pipes under 1200 mm diameter) is maintained in internal BMC OneGIS but restricted from public download.
Measured surveyed invert elevations and silt accumulation levels for over 25,000 roadside stormwater inspection manholes.
Live SCADA telemetry feeds from municipal automated flap gates and sluice valve positions at sea outfalls.
fallback_implementation_details: To achieve 1D-2D coupled hydrodynamic nowcasting, the system must route overland surface runoff using 2D Shallow Water Equations (SWE) on the 30m DEM, while routing subterranean flow through the provided major river/trunk network (links.geojson). For unmapped minor collector drains, an effective synthetic urban drainage network should be derived using hydrological D8/D-infinity flow direction algorithms on the depression-filled DEM, burned along the OpenStreetMap street centerline network (roads.geojson), assuming standard municipal minimum pipe slopes (0.15% to 0.5%) and typical BMC diameter profiles (450mm to 900mm).
source: Brihanmumbai Municipal Corporation (BMC) / Chitale Committee / MMRDA / OSM
license: Public Government Documentation / Open Data Commons ODbL
spatial_resolution: Trunk network (< 5m accuracy); micro-pipes require synthetic fallback
coverage: Greater Mumbai catchment basins (Mithi, Dahisar, Poisar, Oshiwara, Mahim, City outfalls)
quality: medium (High for trunk rivers and pumping stations; partial for minor underground sewers)
limitations: DO NOT assume 100% underground pipe coverage without synthetic drainage derivation. Real-world drainage choking due to solid waste and silt must be modeled via an anomaly decay factor or empirical intake reduction.
processing: Consolidated from official municipal flood reports and satellite tracing of open nullahs into standardized GeoJSON formats.
notes: Essential for 1D Saint-Venant hydraulic routing coupled with 2D overland flow.
